actions.label: Choose a nested column by number
actions.caption: l moves to email first; 1 | selects the first column. Use a counted jump within the nested table.

actions.label: Read the previous nested field
actions.caption: l selects email first; h returns to name. Compare the fields inside this customer object.

actions.label: Read the next nested field
actions.caption: l moves from the customer name to email. Inspect a nested object without leaving its order row.

actions.label: Return to the first nested column
actions.caption: l selects email first; 0 returns to the first column. Reorient yourself inside a nested table.

actions.label: Read the last nested column
actions.caption: $ selects the final nested column. Check email even when a nested object has several fields.

actions.label: Leave the nested chain
actions.caption: esc leaves the nested table and returns to the order table. Continue scanning the surrounding records.

actions.label: Move out one nested level
actions.caption: - leaves one nested level. Step outward gradually when you have drilled through several objects.

actions.label: Show the customer as the main view
actions.caption: D makes the nested customer the main data view. Give its fields more room for closer reading.

notes.note: e opens the file chooser; ctrl+o shows our recent sample files.
Reset point: every action begins here again; earlier actions never change this starting state.
